text:
Alice Kim: Found a frustrating micro-nit in compact density: the drag handle sits on top of the priority pill so the hit area is tiny. Users keep grabbing the pill instead of the handle.
Ben Ho: Repro'd on 1366x768. Two quick options: 1) move handle to the far right in compact; 2) collapse the priority pill into a small icon when dragging. Either keeps the handle accessible.
Priya Nair: +1 for collapsing the pill into an icon during active drag. Also suggest a hover buffer: expand the handle hit area by 8px invisible padding so touch/mouse gets it reliably.
Devon (a11y): Accessibility: ensure the collapsed icon still has a descriptive aria-label like "Priority: 3" and that the drag handle is reachable via keyboard (tab then Space to pick up). For users with `prefers-reduced-motion`, skip the easing and teleport instantly on drop.
Marco Li: Virtual list note: DOM recycling causes the pill->icon swap to flicker. We'll reserve the pill width via CSS `min-width` and swap visual only, not layout, to avoid reflow. Also plan: compute the target slot at drag-start + stable client keys to prevent index jumps.
Jules Rivera: Immersive preview idea: when dragging, the right-hand sim panel should pin to a compact header and hide token counts that overlap the insertion line. That prevents overlays and keeps the insertion guide visible. We can show a small toast in the sim header like "Preview paused while dragging".
Alice Kim: Good call. Also noticed validation toasts sometimes appear behind the sim panel on mobile narrow widths. We should portal to the modal root or use a higher z-index for toasts when preview is active.
Devon (a11y): When portal-ing toasts, mark them role=status and aria-live=polite so screen readers get them without focus theft. For keyboard drag announcements: announce on entry "Move mode enabled" and on each confirmed reposition announce "Moved to position X between 'Auth' and 'Rate Limit'" throttled to 200ms.
Priya Nair: Dev note: add a `dragState` flag to the sim debounce logic so we suspend sim recalculation while dragging, then run once on drop. Reduce noise and CPU.
Ben Ho: Small visual: during drag show a faint dashed insertion line + a micro-bubble with `#N` that uses high-contrast token (#0F172A on white). Confirm color contrast with Claire.
